scope: Nightly 4192 crypto/signing intake: node:crypto and jose moved to effect/crypto, PayloadSigner, AssetSigner, EnvironmentSigningKey/CloudMintSigner, shared DPoP proof creation and a client stream-defect fix. Complete protocol goal remains active.
unchanged: Session, websocket, asset and attachment-upload token layout, claims, HMAC-SHA256 input and signing-key names (server-signing-key, asset-access-signing-key) are byte-identical; signatures are still unpadded base64url.

T3's secret-request ref derivation still keys HMAC with the salt's hex text, so its refs are unchanged. o3's secrets.answerSecretRequest store is private (refs never reach clients) and needs no change; the full request_secret MCP tool/ref lifecycle is still pending.
Desktop bootstrap token derivation (HMAC over t3-desktop-bootstrap:<window>, hex, +-1 window) is unchanged; o3 does not serve that surface.
MCP OAuth client-id and CSRF signing keep the same domain-prefixed payloads; o3 does not serve that surface.
The client-runtime stream-defect change parks a subscription on reported defects instead of ending it; no server wire change.
implemented: Session/websocket and asset/upload grant verification decode payload and signature with Effect Base64Url rules: padded or unpadded, CR/LF stripped, non-zero trailing bits ignored. Tokens split like `const [payload, signature] = token.split(".")`: both non-empty, later segments ignored.

Webhook signature tags decode with Effect Hex (even length, ASCII hex digits only, so Rust's sign-accepting from_str_radix is no longer used) and Base64 (canonical padding, CR/LF stripped, trailing bits ignored), then verify the HMAC over raw body bytes.

validation.directed: auth decoder table matches effect@4.1.2 dist Base64Url/Base64/Hex.decode output for 33 inputs; session verify accepts padded signatures and trailing segments; webhook end-to-end test over the real listener rejects sign-prefixed hex and unpadded base64 and accepts uppercase hex and non-canonical trailing bits (failed on the previous source); asset grants accept padded/trailing-segment variants.
validation.suites: 463 default / 460 without default features, 28 opt-ins ignored each; strict all-target Clippy both modes, fmt, generated compatibility and diff checks.
